shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large upright stone slab/monolith
circular disc/medallion element on the body/torso area
incised linear detailing filling the surface
justification: Both surfaces show low-relief anthropomorphic imagery on a tall upright slab, with an elaborated head/headdress zone at the top, curvilinear scroll motifs, and a prominent circular disc set on the chest/torso region — a reasonably specific shared scheme of a frontal or profile personage bearing a pectoral disc. The biggest difference is that A is a densely filled, multi-register composition of overlapping figures, glyph-like blocks and profile faces spread over the whole panel, whereas B is a single, sculpturally rounded, symmetrical body whose ornament is sparse and organised around a central vertical axis with a belt-like band.
